AIBAST Agents Library

Why the RAPP Brainstem?

It is a local frontier learning and rapid prototyping tool. It is where you learn the agent pattern and prove a prototype on your own machine, before the result graduates into the Microsoft tools that carry it to real users.

What it is

A private practice space where you describe real work in ordinary language and watch GitHub Copilot turn it into a working AI skill. You see the files appear, watch the skill run, review the result, and ask Copilot to improve anything that does not work.

There is no cloud environment to prepare before learning begins. The library's industry solutions and Academy workshops give you realistic starting points, synthetic examples, and visible tests so you can learn by doing rather than by sitting through another presentation.

What it is not

  • Not a replacement for GitHub Copilot. Copilot is the work surface and the model. The Brainstem borrows Copilot's access so there are no keys to manage, and it hands the work back to Copilot the moment you are done learning.
  • Not a competitor to Copilot Studio or Microsoft 365 Copilot. Those are where a finished agent lives. The Brainstem is where the agent is first understood, and the library ships the Copilot Studio solution for every workshop precisely so the prototype can leave.
  • Not a production runtime. Nothing here is built to serve users. It is built to teach one person at a time, quickly.
  • Not another platform to learn. The learner talks to Copilot, watches the work happen, and leaves with a reusable skill. The technical plumbing stays in the background.

Why local, and why "frontier"

The fastest way to learn is to try something, watch it work, change it, and try again. Doing that in a production tenant introduces permissions, publishing, and real-user risk before the learner understands the pattern. Doing it locally keeps the first experiment small, visible, and easy to reset.

Frontier means this is where new AI capabilities are explored first. The supplied workshops use synthetic data and stop before real-world actions. Useful patterns graduate into reviewed solutions. Unhelpful experiments can be discarded without disrupting anyone.

Why it works with the tools people already use

Teams already work across SharePoint, Dynamics, Microsoft 365, local files, and conversations. RAPP does not ask everyone to abandon those tools for one new application. It helps turn a useful way of working into a portable skill that can meet people where they already are.

  • Keep information where it belongs. Learning a workflow does not require copying every source into a new system.
  • Meet people where they work. A proven skill can later appear through Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams, or another experience that fits the user.
  • Give each role the right view. A seller, architect, operator, and leader can use the same underlying capability without needing the same screen or level of detail.
  • Use the AI assistant that fits the moment. Copilot can build the skill, another supported assistant can help inspect or improve it, and the learner keeps the result.

The screen, model, and destination may change. The useful part—the learned workflow and proof that it works—can stay with the person and the team.

Local does not mean isolated

Local-first protects the earliest learning loop: private context stays close to the learner, experiments are inexpensive, and unfinished work is not automatically published. Once something works, the learner can share the skill and its evidence without sharing an entire chat history or private workspace.

  • Personalize locally. Adapt a workspace or agent to a role, account, or workflow without forcing everyone into the same interface.
  • Share deliberately. Share the reviewed skill and safe evidence instead of copying private data or every conversation that produced it.
  • Improve together. A useful local improvement can strengthen the shared version while each person keeps the version that fits their work.

The useful "hive" is not one giant pool of everyone's raw information. It is a team learning from portable capabilities that people intentionally choose to share.

What the learner actually does

  1. Describe the work. Start with a real outcome in ordinary language.
  2. Watch Copilot build it. The files, tools, and decisions remain visible instead of disappearing behind a demo.
  3. Run it immediately. Use synthetic examples to see what the skill does and where it fails.
  4. Improve it through conversation. Correct the result, rerun the test, and watch the capability get better.
  5. Keep the skill. The useful learning becomes a reusable file, not a good answer trapped in yesterday's chat.

Why the learning sticks

A prompt can produce a helpful answer once. RAPP turns the lesson behind that answer into something the learner can see, run, test, change, and reuse. The learner does not have to trust a slide or a polished demonstration—they watch the real workflow complete.

The permanent result is not the conversation. It is the small skill, the decisions that shaped it, and the evidence that it worked. A fresh conversation can pick up that useful context without carrying every stale instruction and detour from the chats that came before.

The graduation path

StageWhereWhat you have at the end
LearnThe Brainstem on your machineA working single-file agent you understand line by line
ProveAcademy workshops and the production guideLocked test cases passing, evidence captured, a reviewed draft
ShipGitHub Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 CopilotThe same learned workflow, adapted for the place your users already work

The library calls these the Brainstem, the Hippocampus, and the Nervous System. The names are a mnemonic for the same idea: start with the survival loop, add memory and a cloud body when you need them, then connect to the enterprise nervous system. You advance when you choose to.

How it stays out of the way

  • No separate model key. The Brainstem uses your existing GitHub Copilot access instead of asking you to create and manage another model-provider credential.
  • Your work is visible. The skill and its local memory are files you can inspect, back up, keep, or delete.
  • Skills stay small. One portable agent file is easier to understand, review, share, and improve.
  • Copilot does the technical work. The learner can stay in conversation while Copilot handles files, tests, and setup in view.
  • You can leave cleanly. The useful learning stays in the skill file rather than being trapped inside the Brainstem.

Who it is for

Sellers, architects, and partners who need to understand an agent pattern well enough to explain it and adapt it, and workshop learners who want to build one before they publish one. If you already know what you want to ship, go straight to the library and take the Copilot Studio solution. If you want to understand it first, install the Brainstem.
